items.duration: Most students finish in three semesters; an extra semester may be needed if switching into CS.
items.credits: 96–108 qualifying units (typically eight courses) plus up to 12 elective units; Systems, Theory, and AI breadth each required.
tracks: Advisor-designed course of study (no fixed specialization list on the MSCS page)
Optional research (~1/3 of students); thesis option
items.coreNotes: Not a fixed core list — construct the plan with an advisor. Must pass one Systems, one Theoretical Foundations, and one AI qualifying course; maintain 3.0 QPA. Many students take 15-213/513.
items.academic: Coursework MS (96–108 qualifying units, typically eight courses) with optional research and a thesis option. Most finish in three semesters; MS admission does not prefer students for the PhD.
items.orientation: Coursework · Optional research · Thesis option · ~3 semesters

items.duration: Up to 3 years / 9 non-summer quarters once the MS CS plan is active; leave of absence counts toward the clock.
items.credits: At least 45 Stanford units on an approved program sheet; ≥8 units per Autumn/Winter/Spring (exceptions for HCP / final quarter).
items.coreNotes: Requirements include Foundations, Significant Software Implementation (SSI), Breadth, Depth (via specialization), and Electives — details on the degree-requirements page. Do not invent a single shared core-course list across specializations.
items.academic: 45-unit MS CS with Foundations, SSI, Breadth, Depth, and Electives on an approved program sheet. Nine predefined specializations (plus rare Individually Designed). Up to three years / nine non-summer quarters.
items.orientation: 45 units · 9 specializations · Coursework or research options

items.duration: One academic year — Fall and Spring only (full-time MEng).
items.credits: Not restated as a single credit total on the EECS MEng overview; program is Fall+Spring with technical concentration, leadership courses, and a team capstone.
items.coreNotes: Industry-oriented MEng (not a research MS). Capstone projects via Fung Capstone Marketplace. Distinguish from research graduate degrees.
items.academic: Full-time EECS MEng completed in one academic year (Fall and Spring) with a technical concentration, engineering leadership coursework, and a team capstone. Concentrations include Data Science, Computer Systems, and Visual Computing among others.

items.duration: On-campus MCS: all requirements within three consecutive fall/spring semesters (Chicago/online MCS up to five years). Research MS: within five consecutive fall/spring semesters.
items.credits: Both MCS and research MS: 32 credit hours. MCS is coursework-only. Research MS: 28 coursework + 4 CS 599 thesis.
items.coreNotes: Catalog routes differ: professional MCS vs research MS with thesis. Breadth + advanced 500-level rules apply; do not invent a single named core-course sequence. Campus Urbana MCS is the primary Fall 2027 catalog route (vs Chicago/online).
items.academic: Siebel School offers a 32-credit professional MCS (coursework-only; Urbana typically ≤3 consecutive semesters) and a separate 32-credit research MS (thesis via CS 599). Eight optional graduate tracks (AI, data science, security, etc.).
items.orientation: MCS or research MS · 32 credits · 8 tracks

items.duration: MS: two-year / four-semester research degree. MEng: principally one-year professional master’s (separate program).
items.credits: MS: 34 credit hours total; 6–12 associated with thesis research (CS 7999); outside minor required. MEng: coursework + capstone (see MEng pages).
items.coreNotes: MS and MEng are distinct. Catalog id covers both routes — prefer stating which route. MS: ≥4 CS courses at 5000+ including ≥1 at 6000+; letter grade C or better.
items.academic: Research MS is a selective four-semester (≈2-year) degree: 34 credits with 6–12 thesis credits, an outside minor, and a written thesis + oral. Professional MEng is a separate ~1-year coursework + capstone route.
items.orientation: MS research thesis · or MEng professional · Distinct routes

items.duration: Must complete within six calendar years (Institute policy). Typical pace not fixed on the overview page — do not invent a semester count.
items.credits: 30 total hours. Default Course Option: 30 coursework. Project Option: 21 coursework + 9 CS 6999. Thesis Option: 18 coursework + 12 CS 7000.
tracks: Human Centered Computing (PhD HCC path note)
items.coreNotes: Exactly one specialization (15–18 hours, grades B+). Remaining free electives. Atlanta campus MSCS cannot use OMSCS online courses. Specialization page lists named core/elective course menus — cite specialization rather than inventing a universal core.
items.academic: Campus MSCS is 30 hours with one required specialization (11 areas; specialization coursework 15–18 hours). Course, Project (9h), or Thesis (12h) options. Complete within six years; keep distinct from OMSCS.

items.credits: 30 credits of coursework; thesis optional. MS and MSE names differ mainly by prior engineering bachelor’s eligibility.
tracks: Field customization via coursework menus in the CSE Graduate Program Guide (not a short fixed specialization list on the overview page)
items.coreNotes: Detailed requirement menus live in the CSE Graduate Program Guide / course-satisfaction sheet — do not invent named cores without that sheet. Thesis optional.
items.academic: CSE master’s requires 30 credits; thesis optional; normally finished in 1.5–2 years. MS vs MSE is primarily naming/eligibility by prior engineering bachelor’s.

items.duration: Designed as about two years for both coursework and thesis options (thesis often finished in the last two semesters; may take longer).
items.credits: Typically 10 courses × 3 credit hours. Breadth 3 + Minor 2; then either 5 electives (coursework) or 3 electives + 2 thesis courses.
items.coreNotes: On-campus research MSCS (not the online MSCS). Breadth and minor course menus are on department pages — do not invent named course lists here. Keep separate from online MSCS.
items.academic: On-campus research MSCS: breadth (3) + minor (2), then coursework (5 electives) or thesis (3 electives + 2 thesis courses); typically ~10 courses / ~2 years. Distinct from the online MSCS.
items.orientation: Research MSCS · Coursework or thesis · ~2 years
